title: Extend perf-canary to benchmark fast/standard/cost-efficient batching tiers across models + GPU SKUs (gate on regressions)
creator: Rina Kobayashi
content:
## Context
We’re introducing workload-aware batching defaults with three SLO tiers: `fast`, `standard`, `cost_efficient`. Runtime changes in this area have a history of causing:
- tail latency regressions (queue delay drift, decode starvation)
- streaming cadence issues (long gaps between tokens)
- SKU-specific behavior differences (H100 vs A100 vs L4)

To make tiered batching safe to ship (and safe to iterate on), we need perf-canary coverage that:
1) runs each tier across a representative set of models and GPU SKUs
2) produces stable comparisons vs baseline
3) fails CI on regressions beyond defined thresholds

This ticket extends perf-canary + benchmark-lab runner to support the tier matrix and adds gating for runtime PRs touching scheduler/batching codepaths.

---

## Goals
- Add perf-canary suites for tiered batching profiles (fast/standard/cost_efficient).
- Benchmark across key model families + SKUs used in Hosted + Dedicated.
- Gate merges/builds on tier-specific regression thresholds (p95, p99, queue delay, streaming cadence).
- Make failures actionable (clear report + links to dashboards/artifacts).

## Non-goals
- Discovering the globally optimal batching params (handled in parameter sweeps + model registry defaults).
- Fully bespoke per-customer tuning.

---

## Proposed matrix (v1)
### Models (v1)
Pick models that represent different prefill/decode characteristics and context length behavior.
- `llama-3-70b` (heavy decode / general purpose)
- `llama-3-8b` (throughput + batching sensitivity)
- `mistral-7b-instruct` (common customer default; smaller model)
- `qwen2-72b` or equivalent “large alt family” (prefill-heavy + different kernel behavior)

Note: actual model IDs should match model registry canonical names used by benchmark-lab.

### GPU SKUs (v1)
- H100 80GB (primary production for large models)
- A100 80GB (still widely deployed; different memory/bandwidth characteristics)
- L4 (cost SKU; sensitive to queue delay/overload)

### Workloads (v1)
- Chat, non-streaming (latency SLO relevant)
- Chat, streaming (cadence sensitive)
- Long-context prefill-heavy scenario (e.g., 8k–16k prompt buckets) *at reduced concurrency*

Workload definitions should reuse the workload corpus runner added in benchmark-lab (see PR link) and the shared corpus doc.

---

## Regression thresholds (initial)
We need thresholds that are strict enough to catch meaningful regressions but not so tight that canary becomes noisy.

### Latency regressions (per tier)
Measured on stable canary runs (N>=3) using the same corpus + concurrency.
- `fast` tier:
  - p95 end-to-end latency: <= +5% vs baseline
  - p99 end-to-end latency: <= +7% vs baseline
- `standard` tier:
  - p95: <= +7%
  - p99: <= +10%
- `cost_efficient` tier:
  - p95: <= +10%
  - p99: <= +12%

### Queue delay regressions
- p95 queue delay: <= +10% vs baseline (all tiers)
- any increase in “queue_delay_ms p99” > +15% triggers “investigate” warning (not a hard fail) until we have more data

### Streaming cadence regressions
For streaming workloads, track:
- time-to-first-token (TTFT) p95
- max inter-token gap p95 (or equivalent cadence metric from runtime spans)

Threshold (initial):
- TTFT p95: <= +5% for `fast`, <= +7% for `standard`, <= +10% for `cost_efficient`
- max inter-token gap p95: <= +10% for `fast` (hard fail), <= +15% for `standard` (soft fail), report-only for `cost_efficient`

### Throughput / utilization guardrails (report-only in v1)
- tokens/sec and GPU util are displayed in report but do not gate in v1.
Reason: too sensitive to background noise + fleet variability; we’ll promote to hard gates after two weeks of stable data.

---

## CI / gating behavior
### When to run
- Nightly scheduled runs on main for the full matrix.
- PR gating for runtime/perf-sensitive changes:
  - Always run for changes in scheduler/batching/KV cache codepaths (label: `perf-sensitive` or path-based trigger)
  - Allow manual re-run command to reduce friction

### What fails the build
- Any hard-fail threshold exceeded for the tier under test.
- If confidence checks fail (high variance / unstable run), mark as “no verdict” and require re-run rather than blocking merge (to avoid flake-based deadlocks).

### Baseline definition
- Baseline is last green run on main for the same SKU/model/workload.
- Store baseline artifacts in the same bucket as existing perf-canary outputs with a stable naming scheme including:
  - runtime commit SHA
  - tier
  - model
  - sku
  - corpus version

---

## Deliverables
1) perf-canary job definitions to run tier matrix (nightly + gated subset).
2) Report template update to include tier comparison table per SKU/model:
   - p50/p95/p99 latency
   - queue delay stats
   - batch size distribution
   - streaming cadence metrics
3) Gating logic with tier-specific thresholds.
4) Triage guidance for common failure modes (queue delay drift, streaming cadence regression, OOM/pressure).

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Nightly perf-canary runs produce results for all tiers across the v1 model+SKU matrix.
- [ ] PR gating triggers on perf-sensitive changes and fails builds on defined regressions.
- [ ] Report artifacts include tier + effective config summary (links to “effective config” endpoint once available).
- [ ] Flake rate acceptable: <10% of scheduled runs marked “no verdict” due to instability.
- [ ] Documented playbook exists in ticket description or linked doc for interpreting failures and next steps.

---

## Implementation plan (proposed)
### ENG-18423-A: Test matrix + runner wiring
- Use benchmark-lab corpus runner to generate the workload patterns.
- Ensure tier selection is passed via config in a consistent way (e.g., `batching_tier=fast|standard|cost_efficient`).

### ENG-18423-B: Reporting + baselines
- Update perf-canary report generator to group results by (tier, sku, model, workload).
- Ensure baseline lookup is stable (same corpus version + same concurrency sweep settings).

### ENG-18423-C: Threshold gating
- Add tier-specific threshold table (config file checked into perf-canary repo).
- Implement hard-fail vs soft-fail categories.

---

## Open questions
1) Do we gate on absolute SLO thresholds (e.g., fast tier must be <X ms) or only regression vs baseline?
   - Proposal: regression-only initially; absolute SLO alerts belong in SRE dashboards.
2) How do we handle model registry changes (new default params) shifting baselines?
   - Proposal: baseline is “last green for same corpus version + same default set”; if defaults change intentionally, bump corpus/config version and re-seed baselines.
3) Streaming cadence metric definition: confirm which metric is stable across runtime versions (span-based vs client-side).

---

## Notes
- This ticket is intentionally scoped to v1 coverage. We should expand matrix post-beta (more regions, more models, more SKUs) once we trust noise characteristics.
- Coordinate with Runtime Scheduling (Sofia) on which PR paths/labels must always run gated canaries.

2025-02-14 (Sahana Iyer): Agree with regression-only gating initially. Absolute SLO checks are too dependent on cluster load. For gating we’ll add a variance check and return “no verdict” (requires rerun) when run-to-run variance is high.

2025-02-18 (Grace Kim): For long-context coverage: please keep concurrency low (e.g., 2/4) and cap max context to avoid turning it into a memory pressure test. We already have separate OOM stress coverage elsewhere.

2025-02-20 (Sofia Ivanova): Important: streaming cadence should be a hard gate for `fast` tier. We already saw decode starvation regressions with fast-tier prioritization experiments. Please include TTFT + max inter-token gap; we can iterate on exact thresholds once we have 1–2 weeks of data.

2025-02-25 (Rina Kobayashi): Implemented grouping in report by (tier, model, sku) locally; needs baseline lookup changes. Also adding a “tier summary” header in the report so it’s obvious which tier failed and why.
2025-02-28 (Sahana Iyer): Hit flakiness in L4 runs due to allocator jitter; adding 3-run median compare for gating and requiring min N=2 successful runs for verdict (otherwise no-verdict).
2025-03-03 (Rina Kobayashi): Wired in benchmark-lab runner output (json) to perf-canary report generator; next step is gating thresholds config + CI wiring for path-based triggers.
2025-03-06 (Sahana Iyer): Opened perf-canary PR with tier suite + gating. Requesting review from Sofia (cadence metrics), Yuki (SKU stability), and Connor (release train impact).

2025-03-08 (Connor O'Brien): Please ensure gating is opt-in for runtime-1.21 branch initially (feature flag in CI) so we can avoid blocking branch cut on unexpected infra noise. Once stable on main for ~1 week, we can flip to default-on gating for perf-sensitive PRs.
